title: Fifth Word The Raw Recruit And The Lesson Of Duty And Prayer

questions.question: What did the careless soldier care about most?
questions.answer: Food and getting what he wanted for himself.

questions.question: What important things did he ignore?
questions.answer: His training and the fighting.

questions.question: Where did he go when he left the group?
questions.answer: He went to the market to buy things.

questions.question: What did his trained friend say was his real job?
questions.answer: To practice and to fight.

questions.question: Why did the friend say he should not worry too much about food?
questions.answer: Because the king would provide for him.

questions.question: Why did the friend say the soldier could not fully take care of himself?
questions.answer: Because he was weak and needy.

questions.question: What could happen if he refused his duty during wartime?
questions.answer: He could be treated like a rebel and be punished.

questions.question: What two kinds of duties did the friend talk about?
questions.answer: The king’s duty to provide and the soldier’s duty to train and fight.

questions.question: In the meaning of the story, what does the battlefield stand for?
questions.answer: This hard and busy worldly life.

questions.question: In the meaning of the story, what does the regiment stand for?
questions.answer: The Muslim community in this time.

questions.question: Who does the good soldier stand for?
questions.answer: A faithful Muslim who does his religious duties.

questions.question: Who does the bad soldier stand for?
questions.answer: A sinful person who chases money and leaves religious duties.

questions.question: In the explanation, what does training stand for first of all?
questions.answer: The daily prayers and worship.

questions.question: What does the war stand for in the lesson?
questions.answer: Fighting against the nafs, bad desires, devils, sin, and bad manners.

questions.question: What are the two big duties of a person in this passage?
questions.answer: To care for life and to worship Allah and trust Him.

questions.question: What is the main lesson from this passage?
questions.answer: We should do our worship and trust Allah instead of forgetting our duties for worldly things.

questions.question: Why was the raw recruit a problem soldier?
questions.answer: He was selfish and did not care about the work he was supposed to do.

questions.question: How did he act about military practice and battle?
questions.answer: He acted like they were not his concern.

questions.question: What did he keep thinking about?
questions.answer: His living and his food.

questions.question: What did that thinking make him do?
questions.answer: It made him leave his unit and go shopping.

questions.question: How did his friend try to correct him?
questions.answer: He reminded him of his duty and told him to trust the king.

questions.question: According to the friend, whose job was it to feed the soldier?
questions.answer: The king’s job.

questions.question: What did the friend mean by saying the soldier was weak and in need?
questions.answer: He meant the soldier could not manage everything by himself.

questions.question: Why was leaving duty even more serious at that time?
questions.answer: Because it was a time of war.

questions.question: What warning did the friend give about disobedience?
questions.answer: The king could punish him for rebelling.

questions.question: What is the worldly place of struggle compared to in the lesson?
questions.answer: A wild place of war.

questions.question: What does the Muslim community of this age represent in the story?
questions.answer: The regiment.

questions.question: What kind of Muslim is shown by the careful soldier?
questions.answer: One who knows and keeps his religious duties and fights his nafs.

questions.question: What kind of person is shown by the careless soldier?
questions.answer: One who is busy only with earning and falls into sins.

questions.question: What does the passage say worship includes first of all?
questions.answer: The prescribed prayers.

questions.question: Besides the nafs, what other enemies are mentioned in the struggle?
questions.answer: Devils from jinn and human beings.

questions.question: What should a believer do toward the Giver of life?
questions.answer: Worship Him, ask from Him, trust Him, and rely on Him.

questions.question: What was wrong with the recruit’s way of thinking?
questions.answer: He cared more about his belly than about his duty.

questions.question: What sentence shows his bad attitude in a simple way?
questions.answer: He thought the hard work was someone else’s problem.

questions.question: What did he do instead of staying with the regiment?
questions.answer: He went out to the market.

questions.question: Who spoke to him and gave him advice?
questions.answer: His trained friend.

questions.question: What did the friend say he had been brought there to do?
questions.answer: To train and to fight.

questions.question: What good quality did the friend tell him to have toward the king?
questions.answer: Trust.

questions.question: Why is trusting the king sensible in the story?
questions.answer: Because the king is the one responsible for feeding him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about doing some jobs for the king?
questions.answer: Sometimes they do service jobs, and the king feeds them for that.

questions.question: What are the soldiers themselves responsible for?
questions.answer: Practice and battle.

questions.question: What danger was the lazy soldier in if he ignored this advice?
questions.answer: He was heading toward trouble and punishment.

questions.question: What does the war place mean in the deeper lesson?
questions.answer: The difficult life of this world.

questions.question: What does the good soldier do against Satan and his nafs?
questions.answer: He struggles against them so he can leave sins.

questions.question: What does the sinful person do while trying to earn a living?
questions.answer: He leaves his religious duties and falls into sins.

questions.question: Why is the inner struggle important in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it protects the heart and spirit from ruin.

questions.question: What is one human duty named near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Supporting life.

questions.question: What is the other human duty named near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Worshipping Allah and trusting Him.

questions.question: What kind of person was the recruit in this story?
questions.answer: He was lazy about duty and focused on himself.

questions.question: What did he pay attention to instead of preparation and battle?
questions.answer: His appetite and his daily needs.

questions.question: How can we tell he did not understand his purpose?
questions.answer: He left his group to chase shopping instead of doing his duty.

questions.question: What did the trained soldier call him in a kind way?
questions.answer: Brother.

questions.question: What lesson did the trained soldier teach first?
questions.answer: That his job was to prepare and fight.

questions.question: What lesson did he teach about rizq, or provision?
questions.answer: That the ruler would not leave him hungry.

questions.question: Why is it foolish to depend only on yourself in the story?
questions.answer: Because a person is needy and cannot handle everything alone.

questions.question: What does the passage say the ruler may do to a disobedient soldier?
questions.answer: Punish him.

questions.question: What does the passage compare this world to?
questions.answer: A rough battlefield.

questions.question: What group is pictured by the regiment?
questions.answer: The Muslim ummah of this age.

questions.question: What is one sign of the good Muslim in the passage?
questions.answer: He carries out his religious duties.

questions.question: What is another sign of the good Muslim in the passage?
questions.answer: He fights against sins and bad desires.

questions.question: What is one sign of the bad person in the passage?
questions.answer: He is swallowed up by worry over earning.

questions.question: What worship act is named as the first part of training?
questions.answer: The five daily prayers.

questions.question: What is the goal of the struggle against sin and bad character?
questions.answer: To save the heart and spirit from everlasting loss.

questions.question: What attitude toward Allah is taught at the end?
questions.answer: To ask from Him, trust Him, and rely on Him.

questions.question: What did the recruit love too much?
questions.answer: His own comfort and food.

questions.question: What did that love stop him from doing well?
questions.answer: His duty.

questions.question: What excuse did he make about training and battle?
questions.answer: He said they were not his business.

questions.question: What did he go out to do?
questions.answer: Buy things in the market.

questions.question: What did his friend say was the reason he was there?
questions.answer: He was there to learn, prepare, and fight.

questions.question: What did the friend tell him to do about fear of hunger?
questions.answer: Leave that worry to the king.

questions.question: In this story, what does that teach us about provision?
questions.answer: We should trust the One who provides.

questions.question: What did the friend say about the time they were living in?
questions.answer: It was a time of war and readiness.

questions.question: Why is neglecting duty dangerous in such a time?
questions.answer: Because it can bring punishment.

questions.question: In the explanation, what does the regiment mean?
questions.answer: The Muslim community.

questions.question: In the explanation, who is like the soldier who does his duty?
questions.answer: A practicing Muslim.

questions.question: In the explanation, who is like the soldier who runs after shopping?
questions.answer: A sinner who leaves worship for worldly gain.

questions.question: What does the passage say training means most of all?
questions.answer: Prayer and worship.

questions.question: What enemies are part of the spiritual battle?
questions.answer: The nafs, its desires, and devils among jinn and people.

questions.question: What is the first duty mentioned near the end?
questions.answer: To preserve and support life.

questions.question: What is the second duty mentioned near the end?
questions.answer: To worship the Lord who gives life and to depend on Him.

questions.question: What habit shows the recruit was not serious?
questions.answer: He kept chasing his own food and shopping.

questions.question: What serious work did he brush aside?
questions.answer: Practice for battle and fighting.

questions.question: What did his friend want him to understand about his mission?
questions.answer: He was there for service and duty, not just for eating.

questions.question: What comfort did the friend give him about being fed?
questions.answer: The king would take care of that.

questions.question: Why did the friend say the recruit should not act proud and independent?
questions.answer: Because he was helpless and needy.

questions.question: What could the king call him if he kept refusing duty?
questions.answer: A rebel.

questions.question: What could happen after that?
questions.answer: He could be punished.

questions.question: What two parts make up the soldier’s life in the friend’s advice?
questions.answer: The ruler provides, and the soldier serves.

questions.question: What does the place of war represent in the lesson for us?
questions.answer: Life in this world with its troubles.

questions.question: What does the passage say the good Muslim knows?
questions.answer: He knows his religious responsibilities and does them.

questions.question: What struggle does the good Muslim carry on?
questions.answer: A struggle against Satan and his own nafs.

questions.question: What happens to the bad person because he is too busy with earning?
questions.answer: He leaves his religious duties and sins.

questions.question: What does prayer belong to in the comparison?
questions.answer: The training and instruction.

questions.question: What is the purpose of fighting the nafs and evil influences?
questions.answer: To be saved from sin, bad manners, and everlasting ruin.

questions.question: Who is called the giver and provider of life in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What should a believer do toward Allah according to the ending of the passage?
questions.answer: Worship Him, ask Him for help, trust Him, and rely on Him.
